hook: David Blei earned an undergraduate degree from Brown University before completing a PhD in computer science at the University of California, Berkeley in 2004, advised by Michael I. Jordan. In 2003, while still a graduate student, he published Latent Dirichlet Allocation together with Jordan and Andrew Ng, introducing a probabilistic model that could uncover hidden topics within large collections of documents. The paper became one of the most cited works in machine learning and gave researchers across many fields a practical tool for organizing and exploring text data. Blei joined the computer science faculty at Princeton University in 2006, building an influential research group focused on Bayesian machine learning and probabilistic modeling. In 2014 he moved to Columbia University, where he holds the William B. Ransford Professorship in Statistics and Computer Science, continuing to develop new methods in variational inference and probabilistic machine learning.
